title: A sandbox cannot run under gVisor, the isolation option for hosts where Firecracker cannot run
foundBy: owner's brief of 2026-11-16 (tasks/sandbox-gvisor-brief.md), written from a hands-on test of runsc release-20261109.0 under rootless Podman 5.8.9 on Fedora 44
stint: gvisor branch, session agent working the owner's brief, 2026-11-16
details:
A sandbox is either a rootless Podman container, which shares the host kernel, or a Firecracker microVM, which needs KVM. Cloud machines without nested virtualization and most CI runners can offer only the first. With gVisor's `runsc`, a container's system calls run in a kernel written in user space. That narrows what the container reaches of the host kernel, without hardware virtualization.

The owner pointed Podman at `runsc` through `CONTAINERS_CONF_OVERRIDE` and ran the unmodified `cs-sandbox create --engine podman`. Create, `exec`, ssh from the host and between peers, the toolchains, and `group rm` all worked. Three things did not, and this session measured why:

- **No start without `--ignore-cgroups`.** Rootless `runsc` asks systemd's system bus for its cgroups and is refused (`Access denied as the requested operation requires interactive authentication`). With the flag it starts, and every limit `create` sets applies to nothing.
- **`sudo` fails** with `effective uid is not 0`. runsc carries the reason in its own strings: `--allow-suid is disabled, SUID/SGID bits on executables will be ignored`. A sandbox started with `--allow-suid` runs `sudo -n true`, and one started without it fails.
- **Nested containers fail** with `failed to bind mount ns ... invalid argument`. Under strace, the nested podman calls `mount("/proc/thread-self/ns/net", ..., MS_BIND|MS_REC|MS_SHARED)`. Linux ignores the propagation flag beside `MS_BIND`. gVisor returns `EINVAL`, and the same call with `MS_BIND` alone succeeds. A nested container on the sandbox's own network namespace runs.

The work is to offer gVisor as an engine of its own, fetch `runsc` the way the VMM is fetched, and fix or name each of the three.

notes.text:
Commit 3f6a939 adds `--engine gvisor`, and e338037 and 7f153ba refine what it says. The first `create`, or `build --engine gvisor`, fetches runsc release 20261109.0 into the artifact cache. It checks the archive against a SHA-512 committed in `internal/gvisor`. The container runs under a wrapper that passes `--ignore-cgroups`, `--allow-suid`, `--net-raw` and `--oci-seccomp`.

A systemd user scope under `cs-sandbox.slice` holds conmon, the gofer and the Sentry. It carries `--pids`, `--cpus` and `--mem` as TasksMax, CPUQuota and MemoryMax, and is made again on every start. Under gVisor the entrypoint gives the nested engine `netns = "host"`. So `sudo` and the limits are fixed. Nested containers run on the sandbox's own network, which `create` and the documents say.

Verified on this host, Fedora 44 with kernel 7.3.3 and rootless Podman 5.8.9. `make ci` passed over the working tree that became 3f6a939, and again over the one that became 7f153ba. In both runs TestCLIGVisorLive passed its running, nested and restart subtests. `make test-agents-replay AGENTS_ENGINE=gvisor` passed all six cells, lent and shared.

By hand, `--repo`, `--snapshot`, `fetch`, `push`, `forward` and peer ssh all worked. Walkthrough 4's nginx answered on port 80 and not on 8080, as documented. In a probe scope, a 1.5 GiB allocation under a 1 GiB MemoryMax ended the sandbox with exit 137. TasksMax=200 did the same to a guest that started 400 processes.

Measured against a Podman sandbox at the same time, with the host's load average near 11. Writing 5,000 small files ran 2.5 times slower in the root filesystem and 7 times slower in the home. A small Go build ran 1.6 times slower, and starting 300 processes 6 times slower.

Nothing here ran on GitHub CI, arm64, WSL2 or macOS. Host-route, image stores and gVisor's KVM platform are untested. CI does not fetch runsc yet, so TestCLIGVisorLive skips there, and this stays open until a run covers it.

Commit af200a5 makes `make setup-smoke` run `cs-sandbox build --engine gvisor` on a Linux host with podman, when SMOKE_TESTS names TestCLIGVisorLive. CI's ubuntu-26.04, ubuntu-26.04-arm and WSL2 smoke legs all run setup-smoke, so each now fetches the pinned release and checks its digest. The ubuntu-26.04 job prints `doctor --engine gvisor` and the AppArmor userns setting first. Local make ci over that tree fetched runsc inside setup-smoke, and TestCLIGVisorLive passed its three subtests.

The branch is not pushed, so no CI run has executed the member yet. This stays open until one passes it.
